subject: Dedicated capacity — throttling, metering & credit approach
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Morris <j.morris@acme-bio.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool pricing and handling spikes

Hi Janelle —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I promised a short note that focuses on how Redwood handles above-commit usage for Dedicated GPU pools and the practical options we typically offer customers in pilot/early-production phases.

Attached: RBW-Proposal-Acme-Dedicated-v1.pdf (proposal + baseline sizing worksheet)

Quick summary:
- Baseline commit: reserved GPU pool sized for your expected sustained throughput (example in attached worksheet).
- Short bursts: we support a configurable burst buffer so intermittent spikes don’t immediately translate to failed requests.
- Metering & billing: all tokens/processing are metered; billing reconciles committed capacity vs. above-commit usage per billing window.
- Throttling policy: soft throttle (queuing) applied when burst buffer is exhausted; hard throttle only beyond safety thresholds to protect other tenants in shared infra (rare for Dedicated).
- Credits & grace: for initial ramp we typically offer a bootstrapping credit or waived overage for N days to allow load shaping.

I realize the devil’s in the details — could you tell me which of the following matters most for your procurement/security teams so I can surface exact wording?
1) Predictability: max monthly $ cap vs. per-hour overage rate
2) SLA/throughput guarantees: do you need guaranteed P95 latency at sustained peaks?
3) Credit windows: do you prefer an upfront one-time credit or multi-month amortized credits?

If you’d like, I can propose 2-3 concrete billing options (with numbers) for review by procurement.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0219

From: Janelle Morris <j.morris@acme-bio.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pricing and handling spikes

Camila —

Appreciate the summary and the proposal. A few clarifying questions from procurement and infra:

- How do you differentiate throttling vs. burst buffer in practice? If we have a day with sustained 1.8x traffic for 6 hours, what happens?
- What does "metered" mean at the invoice level? Is it per-GPU-hour, per-token, or a blended metric? We need line items we can present to finance.
- Are there automatic ways to convert sustained above-commit into a higher commit mid-cycle (prorated)? That would help us avoid surprise overage invoices.
- You mentioned credits for a ramp period — what are typical magnitudes and eligibility?

Also, security asked to see formal wording for throttling and hard-fail cases so their engineers can plan fallbacks.

Can you send two numbered options: (A) conservative — minimal risk of throttling (higher commit + smaller burst), (B) economical — smaller commit + burst with stricter metering/credits model. We’ll share with procurement next week.

Thanks,
Janelle
Janelle Morris
Head of ML Infrastructure, Acme Bio
j.morris@acme-bio.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated pool pricing and handling spikes — negotiation notes (internal)

Marissa/Laura —

Looping you in with Janelle’s asks (below). They want two concrete options and formalized throttling language for security. Procurement cares about clear invoice line items and the ability to upgrade mid-cycle.

My proposed approach (numbers as placeholders for internal approval):

Option A (Conservative / Low throttle risk)
- Commit: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (monthly).
- Burst buffer: 10% free burst (auto-queued short spikes).
- Overrun handling: soft queue up to 10% beyond buffer for up to 15 minutes; sustained >10% enters hard-throttle.
- Pricing: base rate $X per GPU-hour; overage billed at 1.5x base rate beyond buffer.
- Discount: 12% on base rate for a 12-month commit.

Option B (Economical / Burst-first)
- Commit: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved.
- Burst buffer: 20% free burst for first 30 days (bootstrap).
- Overrun handling: soft queue then proportional shedding; hard-throttle beyond sustained 20% for >2 hours.
- Pricing: base rate $Y per GPU-hour; overage billed at 1.2x base rate but with credit-for-sustained-overage (see credits below).
- Discount: 8% on base rate for 12-month commit.

Credits & ramping (proposal):
- 30-day onboarding credit: waiver of overage charges up to 20% burst for first 30 days.
- Sustained overage credit: if >15% sustained overage for 2 consecutive billing cycles, we apply a 50% credit on cumulative overage for one cycle while we review commit size upgrade.
- Mid-cycle commit upgrade: allowed with 24-hour notice; prorated commit billing for remainder of cycle.

Why this is safe: the soft queue preserves latency for short spikes; hard-throttle thresholds protect the pool and other customers in multi-tenant scenarios (rare for Dedicated but we keep safety rails).

Action: need approval to present these two options and offer a one-time 10% startup credit (applies to first invoice) — Marissa/Laura, are you comfortable with this as a standard light-weight concession for strategic pilots?

Attachment: proposed-credit-matrix.xlsx (pricing/credit calculus)

Camila

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Morris <j.morris@acme-bio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pricing and handling spikes

Hi Janelle —

Thanks for the clear asks. We pulled together two concrete options and the formal wording security requested for throttling/overage handling. Below is the abbreviated summary; I attached a one-page overage summary for procurement.

Option A — Conservative (recommended if predictability is the priority)
- Reserved commit: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (monthly).
- Burst buffer: 10% automatic burst (short spikes).
- Behavior on spikes: up to buffer = no billing change; buffer exhausted = soft queue for up to 15 minutes; sustained >10% beyond buffer => hard throttle to protect throughput guarantees.
- Billing: invoice shows base commit line item (GPU-hours) + line item for overage (per-GPU-hour at 1.5x base).
- Discount: 12% for 12-month commit.

Option B — Economical (recommended for pilots with variable load)
- Reserved commit: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (monthly).
- Burst buffer: 20% free burst for first 30 days (onboarding waiver).
- Behavior on spikes: soft queuing followed by proportional shedding; sustained >20% beyond buffer for >2 hours triggers hard throttle.
- Billing: base commit + overage (per-GPU-hour at 1.2x base) with credit mechanics for sustained overage (see below).
- Discount: 8% for 12-month commit.

Credits & ramp rules (applies to both options)
- 30-day onboarding waiver: overage up to stated burst % waived for first 30 days.
- Sustained-overage remediation: if sustained >15% above commit for two consecutive billing cycles, we apply a one-time 50% credit on that accumulated overage while we agree a commit adjustment.
- Mid-cycle upgrades: allowed with 24-hour notice; commit increases prorated for that billing cycle.

Throttling & hard-fail language for security (copyable):
- "Redwood will apply soft queuing for transient bursts up to the configured burst buffer. If sustained usage exceeds configured thresholds (defined per-customer at provisioning), Redwood will employ proportional shedding to maintain cluster health. Persistent breaches beyond the configured hard-throttle threshold may result in request rejection until usage returns below thresholds. Redwood will provide advance notification to the customer's designated contacts if hard-throttle actions are expected or performed."

Next steps:
- If procurement prefers Option A or B, we’ll produce a formal SOW and amended pricing schedule.
- I’m authorized to offer a one-time 10% startup credit to reduce first-invoice friction (applies to base commit charge).

Attached: redwood-dedicated-overage-summary.pdf (one-page, procurement-ready)

Happy to hop on a short call with procurement and engineering to walk through the exact invoice lines/security wording.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
